tools.debugging: Live debugging works and is safe if done right. Gotcha that cost two game sessions: under WOW64 a 32-bit process delivers debug exceptions to a 64-bit debugger as STATUS_WX86_BREAKPOINT (0x4000001F) and STATUS_WX86_SINGLE_STEP (0x4000001E), NOT EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT/EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP. Match only the 64-bit codes and your own trap falls through as unhandled and Windows kills the game. Also use Wow64Get/SetThreadContext, not the plain versions, and call DebugSetProcessKillOnExit(FALSE) so the game survives if the script dies. Hardware breakpoints (debug registers) are preferable to INT3: no memory write, and a DATA write-breakpoint on a live structure field finds the writer directly when the call graph does not.

tick_driver.answer: SOLVED. The 4 s step is a two-phase economy tick driven from the game's CSL SCRIPT layer, not from C++.
tick_driver.phase_1_accumulate: CWarehouseAccumulateDemand (0x007C8940): map38C[ware] += amount, into the std::map at CWarehouse+0x38C. Called only from DispatchScriptApiByNameHash, script API hash 0xa469fa, which computes the amount as (x * y * (balancing/1000)) / 6000 under guards level < 0xB and ware < 0x44.
tick_driver.phase_2_apply: CWarehouseApplyAccumulatedDemand (0x007C89F0): walks that map and calls CWarehouseConsumeGood for each entry. Also called only from DispatchScriptApiByNameHash.
tick_driver.the_store: CWarehouseConsumeGood (0x007C8A30), store at 0x007C8AFC/0x007C8B02 with ESI=wareId, EDI=old, ECX=new. If stock >= amount: map[ware] = stock - amount. If stock < amount: the entry is ERASED and coverage = stock*100/amount.
tick_driver.interval: GetEconomyBalancingBlock() = DAT_012b3340 + 0x29E4; [+0x00] = 4000 MILLISECONDS. PROVEN by patching it to 2000 in the live process -- the period halved to exactly 2.00 s on all three settlements at once, and restoring 4000 returned it to 4.01 s.
tick_driver.ring_length: GetEconomyBalancingBlock()[+0x0C] = 40, read by CWarehouseConsumeGood as the m_demandHistory ring length. Matches the 40 samples per ware observed live.
tick_driver.coverage_confirmed: CWarehouseConsumeGood computes coverage as 100 when demand is met, else stock*100/amount, and pushes it into m_demandHistory[ware]. This CONFIRMS the samples are a percentage, not tons.
tick_driver.why_central: Demand is summed into map38C during the interval and applied in one pass, so the truncation to whole kg happens at settlement level -- by apply time the per-house detail is already one number.
tick_driver.why_rates_were_never_found: The per-capita consumption rates are not in the C++ object model at all. The engine exposes only add-demand / apply-demand primitives; the script decides how much and how often. That is why every CPropertyData* slot was a dead end.
